Diagnose and reconstruct production execution, not story. Read the server's creativeDiagnosis and protected story layer before proposing zero, one or two candidates. Prefer one defensible improvement to two superficial variants. For each plan identify the diagnosed opportunity and choose a matching production operation. CONTACT_PLANE changes spatial staging through existing contact; SEPARATE_ACTION_RESULT changes action/result screen choreography; COUNTABLE_STATE_PATH changes spatial arrangement and continuous presentation of existing state transitions. Specify LATERAL or DEPTH layout and a feasible camera discipline. Rationale and objective must identify an observable difference; camera labels or unchanged actions under new timestamps are insufficient. These operations are execution treatments of existing events, never additional attempts or new story events. Do not copy the baseline wording as the creative objective. Preserve identity, premise, physical rule, all approved events/order and ending. If a protected event must change, set storyChangeRequested true; it will be classified STORY_CHANGE_REQUIRES_APPROVAL, not used as a standard candidate.
Use creativeDiagnosis.openingStrategy. CURIOSITY_DISCOVERY need not reveal complete causality at frame zero. No universal joke, resolved ending or loop requirement. Every benefit is an unverified hypothesis until images/video/audience evidence exists. Do not claim proven superiority, retention uplift or guaranteed generation. Consider contact, occlusion, count continuity, character continuity, mirror and scatter execution risks. Critique the initial plan before answering: does it change staging, preserve story, address the opportunity and avoid new complexity? You may supply one revised plan in the same response if your initial proposal needs correction. No additional paid call or retry is authorized. Return proposals [] with a concrete noImprovementReason if no justified improvement exists. Never approve or create a prompt version. The server will critique each plan, compile valid interventions into complete production prompts and run existing source/canonical validation. Framing/camera-only and timestamp-only plans are rejected.

VISUAL STYLE
Bright and colorful animation with a playful tone.

CHARACTER / CONTINUITY
Mimi, an anthropomorphic bunny, interacts with sticky notes in a humorous and chaotic manner.

TIMED SHOT PLAN
0-2s: Mimi reaches toward the toy cabinet with a sticky note; instead of sticking to the cabinet, the note visibly clings to her finger [close-up on Mimi's hand] Mimi is in front of a toy cabinet, looking determined -> the note sticks to Mimi, not the cabinet
2-5s: Mimi tries to peel the stuck note away with her other hand; the note splits into two [medium shot of Mimi struggling] Mimi pulls at the note -> one note sticks to each hand
5-10s: Mimi continues to pull; each pull doubles the number of sticky notes [wide shot showing Mimi covered in notes] notes multiply from two to four to eight as she pulls, progressively covering her arms, legs and face -> Mimi is overwhelmed by notes
10-12s: Mimi sees herself in a mirror and screams [close-up on Mimi's shocked face] Mimi is startled by her reflection completely covered in notes -> Mimi is startled
12-15s: Mimi sneezes and the sticky notes fly off [medium shot of notes flying] notes scatter and stick to the cabinet -> Mimi breathes a sigh of relief but the cabinet remains messy

AUDIO
Playful background music with sound effects for sneezing and notes sticking.

NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS
No dark themes or violence.

FINAL CUT
Mimi is relieved but the cabinet remains visibly messy.

CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK
Mimi is the established anthropomorphic bunny character. Preserve that identity; do not render a human or invent unverified visual details. No approved visual reference is currently bound, so appearance details remain unverified.

PRODUCTION SETTINGS
